insights: Space and robotics topics are the most reliable traffic drivers, consistently reaching 1,000+ views on Shorts, whereas niche environmental or infrastructure topics (like undersea cables or cloud seeding) struggle below 400 views.
'Myth vs fact' and 'Shocking fact first' styles yield the highest retention, regularly exceeding 70% to 150% average view duration (e.g., Europa Clipper at 155% and Artemis III at 114%).
A critical drop-off consistently occurs between 4.5 and 8.5 seconds across Shorts, signaling that opening lines must immediately state the payoff rather than setting up slow context.

Explicit channel promotions and teasers (such as 'The full breakdown is on our channel' or 'Follow Tomorrowly') trigger severe audience drop-offs of up to 23%; loops and cliffhangers should replace formal sign-offs.
Community engagement is critically low (0 to 2 comments across virtually all videos), indicating that current endings lack open-ended, debatable questions to prompt comments.
Data for long-form videos is too thin (only 5 uploads, median 85 views) to determine clear long-form patterns, though currently Shorts feed accounts for 80-95% of incoming reach.
